scope: Fixed-package RSS attribution and one-hour health; no backend/frontend changes or deployment.

resources.workload: 32 routes, no TLS, small GET responses, one client IP, replenish/capacity 10000, cost1, allow/allow, handoff false, 8 workers + queue128

config.note: RSS investigation: same full capacity plan; read-only checkpoints every five minutes during the soak and idle. No forced GC, trim or restart.

limiter.commandCountMeaning: Client dispatches without an observed result or a confirmed physical close, including probes; excludes decoding and downstream work. Not a Redis-server running-command count.

observations.note: Cumulative, non-atomic local observations. Durations include scheduling and GC; command observation is not Redis server execution time. Post-decision cancellation does not undo the quota decision.

saturationEvents.note: Rejection-triggered, rate-limited, non-atomic local observations. At most 256 retained tasks inspected and 8 oldest detailed. No IP or request ID. Thread state and GC counters do not prove scheduler causality.

limits: Within-process trim demonstrates reclaimable allocator pages only; no exact allocation-owner identification.
Native allocator free bytes and NMT committed are not RSS and must not be added.
Different conditioning duration and JVM history prohibit an inter-run causal comparison.

nativeAllocator.measurement: glibc malloc_info, allocator accounting, not RSS or NMT

toolTests.classification: deterministic unit/process fixtures, not a substitute for live load

validation.live: Two isolated experiments with actual gateway, Redis, upstream, driver, response-version coverage, per-sample sync, health/accounting and real container-exit gates.
notExecuted: Backend 259-test suite and production rebuild: fixed verified byte-identical JAR; no backend code changed.
Full prior proxy/limiter/config failure matrices: no relevant product change; historical evidence only checked.
Repeat one-hour sample, multi-hour natural plateau or 4000 req/s trial.
Full GC, heap dump, object retention graph, JFR or allocator replacement.
NMT-off overhead control; current health includes diagnostic cost.

cleanup.desktop: Left running, same as this task initial environment; no existing container started or upgraded.

environmentAssessment.cause: Unknown. Default bridge identity also changed in earlier independent reviews; this run does not establish the cause. Original failure is preserved, not normalized to success.
environmentAssessment.experimentNetwork: Both runs used their own named, owner-labeled networks. No command targeted removal/recreation of the default bridge.
environmentAssessment.effect: Container resource limits were fixed and recorded. Cross-run environment identity is not proven; no causal comparison of absolute RSS between JVMs.
environmentAssessment.followup: No further Docker mutation or experiment in this scope. Record the environment difference for separate investigation.

methods.timing: Original UTC timestamps retained; no host clock changes.
methods.measurements: Heap used/committed, NMT committed, RSS and cgroup overlap and are not additive.
methods.gc: Natural young-GC after-use is not an exact live-object census.
methods.nativeIntervention: Exactly one explicit native trim in experiment02 after healthy conditioning and drain; outside capacity/natural observation. No forced GC in either run.
methods.sampledPeaks: Finite-frequency observations; limiter lifetime peaks reported separately.
methods.bounds: Fixed 4 logical CPUs/1GiB, small GETs/no TLS, nonpersistent single Redis; no production capacity extrapolation.
